properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Alex (who:alex), relayed by Anthony, 2026-09-23, about his workplace project (recorded without the employer or domain).

HIS WORDS, the parts that carry the idea:
· "I really want to pare down the amount of info that is in the graph. I think I was over aggressive in documenting too much. It's more about documenting the capabilities and requirements that the app fulfills and where they are. It's too many tokens to categorize this otherwise and too much time."
· "The code is not the important part. It's the 10k decisions on why we did things over 6 years that cannot be deduced by a computer that matter. Our AI agents are extremely adept at finding their way through the code bases and making changes. I want to provide the historical context from the 10k hours I've worked on this project."
· Asked whether the commit history could supply it: "The commit history does not have the context I want to provide."
· His process: "It'll look at the code and say there is a button here that downloads some artifact. And I'll say yeah, that was needed because user profile X had Y need for it. And then repeat that like a bazillion times."

⭐⭐ WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT WHAT A DESIGN IS FOR, ON A MATURE PROJECT. For him the code is the one thing that does NOT need recording: agents navigate it well. What is irrecoverable is intent: who needed each thing and why it is shaped the way it is. That is reflow2's own founding claim (intent is what the code cannot tell you), met in a field user's words with no prompting.

⭐ AND IT ALREADY HONOURS ADOPT'S CENTRAL DISCIPLINE. The adopt skill's rule is "never infer a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it". In his loop the code only supplies the QUESTION (what is this?); the requirement comes from the owner. Everything around that is where it parts company with the skill as served, which is structure-first: "Model the whole repo, not a region", both sides of every contract, nest every part, a Fragment per source, a checksum per code artifact, intent recovered in Phase 3 after the structure exists.

THE SHAPE HE IS DESCRIBING, in reflow2's terms: per feature — a Capability (what it does, status realized) with a pointer to where it lives (an Artifact at file or directory granularity, or a location on the capability); a Requirement stating the need, with `source` naming the user profile (an Actor) and the owner's word behind it; SATISFIES between them; and a Decision when the answer is "we chose X over Y because". Almost all of it exists; `add_requirement` gained `source` in v0.67.0.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:

(a) AN INTENT-INTERVIEW MODE OF ADOPT (or a sibling skill). The agent walks the code, lists what it visibly does in the owner's terms, and asks why; each answer lands as the chain above in one call. No Interfaces, no nesting, no checksums, no Fragments unless asked. Structure only as coarse "where it lives" pointers.

(b) BATCH THE QUESTIONS so "a bazillion" becomes pages: the agent proposes ten or twenty features at once with its best reading of each, and the owner answers in one message ("3 is for the auditors, 7 was a customer escalation, skip 12"). The gap walkthrough already does this for detector findings and a field user answered 16 questions in one reply.

(c) CHOOSE WHAT TO ASK ABOUT, rather than asking about everything: user-facing surface first (screens, routes, exports, reports), or what changed most, or the owner's own list of the parts with the most history. Coverage then grows where the history is richest.

(d) THE STRUCTURAL HALF MADE MECHANICAL AND CHEAP, so tokens go only to the interview. req:adopt-can-take-a-code-graph-as-its-mechanical-structural-pass (accepted 2026-09-23) is this, and dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest argued for it from determinism; Alex's cost figure (fact:ingesting-a-real-workplace-corpus-costs-70-dollars-a-day-and-still-writes-duplicate-components) is the money argument it lacked. For Alex (d) may be optional: he may not want the structure at all.

(e) ADOPT ASKS ITS SCOPE FIRST: "is this design for controlling the system's structure, or for keeping why it is the way it is?" — and runs only the phases that answer. A one-question fork at the start, recorded as a project-level decision.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea:
· WITHOUT STRUCTURE, SOME CHECKS GO QUIET. Gap detection about unallocated or uncontracted parts has nothing to run on. For his purpose that may be correct; it should be said, not discovered.
· "WHERE IT LIVES" ROTS. A pointer to a file moves when the code does. Directory-level or module-level pointers rot slower; checksums would catch movement but are exactly the cost he wants to drop.
· A BAZILLION IS STILL A BAZILLION. Batching and choosing reduce the owner's time per answer, not the number of answers his 10k decisions need. The honest target is the history that matters, not all of it.
· PRUNING WHAT HE ALREADY HAS is a separate need ("pare down"): an existing over-detailed design needs a way to retire the structural layer without losing the intent attached to it. Not designed here.

CORRECTION 2026-09-23 (Anthony, the same day): "I don't think he ever ran adopt to be honest." So Alex's over-capture did NOT come from following the adopt skill's structure-first instructions, and nothing above should be read as saying it did. The comparison with the skill still stands as a statement about the skill as served, and matters for the next adopter; it is not evidence about Alex's session.

What this changes:
· THE QUESTION BEHIND "over aggressive in documenting" IS OPEN: by what route did he capture (genesis, corpus ingest, hand-driven capture sentence by sentence), and what in that route pushed toward documenting everything? Not asked of him yet; only he can say.
· IT IS ALSO A DISCOVERABILITY DATA POINT: a user bringing an existing, six-year-old system under reflow2 did not reach the skill written for exactly that case. Whether adopt would have helped or hurt him is a separate matter; that he did not find it is itself worth knowing.
· HIS LOOP (the agent names a feature, he says why) is closer to option (a) than to anything adopt prescribes today, which strengthens (a) as a mode in its own right rather than a trimmed adopt.

📌 CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-09-23: the same day, dec:idea-a-change-justification-skill-walks-the-commit-history-and-asks-why proposed the historical counterpart (why did each change happen, from the commit history). Its recorded RECOMMENDATION (the hub agent's, not a decision) is that this feature interview and that change walk become ONE skill with two walks, separate from adopt and pointed to by it, working name `/why`. Read there for the reasoning, including Anthony's framing: adopt recovers the implemented and fielded half by reverse engineering; this recovers the concept and decision half from the design lead who holds it.



BUILT IN PART 2026-09-23: option (a) as a SIBLING skill rather than a mode of adopt — the feature walk of the `why` skill (chg:the-why-skill-records-why-an-existing-system-is-the-way-it-is) — with (b) pages answered in one message and (c) the owner choosing the order. Adopt's Phase 3 now points to it. Still open here: (e), adopt asking its purpose first, and pruning a design that already holds too much.
properties.name: OPEN — should adopt have an intent-first mode: the agent names what the code visibly does, the owner says WHY (which user, which need), and the design records only capabilities, requirements, the decisions behind them and where they live — no structural model?
